## Overview

Revives #43208 by @markmc, which @robertgshaw2-redhat approved before it was closed for inactivity: a "Drain Shutdown" section in the Kubernetes deployment guide covering `--shutdown-timeout`, a `preStop` hook and `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`. It applies the two review suggestions on that PR and corrects what I found to differ from the server's behavior while testing drains with `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` on Kubernetes-style `SIGTERM` (sent to PID 1 with `docker kill`).

## Changes from #43208

| #43208 | This PR | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Example runs `/bin/sh -c "vllm serve ..."` | Passes the model and flags as `args` to the image's `vllm serve` entrypoint, and explains why | The shell becomes PID 1 and does not forward `SIGTERM`, so vLLM never starts draining and the pod is killed at the grace period (the `exec` suggestion in review) |
| "A second SIGTERM will skip the drain timeout" | Removed | `serve_http` ignores further signals once shutdown has started (`if shutdown_event.is_set(): return`); skipping the drain on a second signal is the gRPC server's behavior (#62967) |
| New requests during the drain "return 503" | "The server stops taking new requests", without a status code | On a single API server they currently fail with 500 (`cannot schedule new futures after shutdown`); with #61562 they are refused at the socket |
| `/health` and `/metrics` "remain accessible during drain" | Replaced by a note not to rely on the readiness probe during the drain | `/health` reports engine liveness, not drain state; documenting it as available suggests the readiness probe takes the pod out of rotation, which is what the `preStop` sleep is for |
| `terminationGracePeriodSeconds >= preStop + --shutdown-timeout` (60 = 15 + 45 in the example) | Adds a teardown margin; example uses 15 + 40 + 15 = 70 | The engine and the server need time to exit after the drain (the margin suggestion in review); #64991 gives EngineCore 5 s past the timeout |
| Timeout sized from token throughput | Keeps that, and points to the p99 of `vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds` | Lets operators size it from their own traffic |
| | Notes that aborted requests end with `finish_reason="abort"` when the abort reaches the client, and that clients should treat it as incomplete | Observed with `--shutdown-timeout 0`; the drain-deadline case is left until #64991 lands |

## Validation

- Behaviors above checked on `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (0.33.0rc1.dev421+g2b009fc6d), RTX 5060 Ti, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `--shutdown-timeout 0` and `20`, `SIGTERM` to PID 1 via `docker kill`; the signal-handling claim against `serve_http` in `vllm/entrypoints/launchers/launcher.py`.
- `pre-commit` (markdownlint) passes on `docs/deployment/k8s.md`.

**AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude) was used to review #43208 against the experiments above and draft the text. I reviewed every line and ran the experiments myself.

Co-authored with @markmc (original section in #43208).

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.

</details>

@@ -468,6 +469,99 @@ This server does not enable gRPC reflection, so check a service manually with [`
 grpc_health_probe -addr=localhost:50051 -service=readiness
 ```
 
+## Drain Shutdown
+
+For production deployments, vLLM can drain in-flight requests before it exits, so rolling updates and scale-downs do not cut off requests that are still generating.
+
+### How It Works
+
+When the vLLM process receives `SIGTERM` (sent by Kubernetes when a pod terminates):
+
+1. The server stops taking new requests.
+1. In-flight requests keep running until they finish, for at most `--shutdown-timeout` seconds.
+1. The engine and the server exit.
+
+### Configuration
+
+Enable drain shutdown by setting `--shutdown-timeout` to a non-zero value:
+
+| Argument                     | Default | Description                                                             |
+|------------------------------|---------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
+| `--shutdown-timeout=0`       | Yes     | Immediate shutdown: in-flight requests are aborted on `SIGTERM`         |
+| `--shutdown-timeout=SECONDS` |         | Drain shutdown: wait up to SECONDS for in-flight requests to complete   |
+
+With `--shutdown-timeout=0`, an aborted request ends with `finish_reason` set to `"abort"` (followed by `data: [DONE]` when streaming) if the abort reaches the client before the engine process exits; otherwise the connection closes mid-response. Clients should treat either outcome as an incomplete answer rather than a finished one.
+
+### Example Deployment
+
+`SIGTERM` has to reach the vLLM process itself. The `vllm/vllm-openai` image runs `vllm serve` as its entrypoint, so pass the model and flags as `args`. Wrapping the command in `/bin/sh -c` makes the shell the container's main process; the shell does not forward `SIGTERM`, so the drain never starts and the pod is killed when `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` runs out. If you need a shell, start vLLM with `exec vllm serve ...`.
+
+The example uses a `preStop` hook to delay `SIGTERM`, giving Kubernetes time to remove the pod from the Service endpoints before the drain begins. The three timeouts relate as follows:
+
+```text
+terminationGracePeriodSeconds >= preStop sleep + --shutdown-timeout + margin
+```
+
+The margin covers the engine's teardown and the process exit after the drain; leave at least 10 seconds.
+
+<details>
+<summary>Yaml</summary>
+
+```yaml
+apiVersion: apps/v1
+kind: Deployment
+metadata:
+  name: vllm-server
+spec:
+  replicas: 3
+  selector:
+    matchLabels:
+      app: vllm
+  template:
+    metadata:
+      labels:
+        app: vllm
+    spec:
+      # 15 s preStop + 40 s drain + 15 s margin
+      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 70
+      containers:
+      - name: vllm
+        image: vllm/vllm-openai:latest
+        # The image's entrypoint is `vllm serve`, which then receives SIGTERM directly.
+        args: ["mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3", "--shutdown-timeout", "40"]
+        ports:
+        - containerPort: 8000
+        lifecycle:
+          preStop:
+            exec:
+              command: ["/bin/sleep", "15"]
+        livenessProbe:
+          httpGet:
+            path: /health
+            port: 8000
+          initialDelaySeconds: 60
+          periodSeconds: 10
+        readinessProbe:
+          httpGet:
+            path: /health
+            port: 8000
+          initialDelaySeconds: 60
+          periodSeconds: 5
+        resources:
+          limits:
+            nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
+```
+
+</details>
+
+### Key Considerations
+
+- **`terminationGracePeriodSeconds`**: When it runs out, Kubernetes kills the pod regardless of the drain. Keep it above the `preStop` sleep plus `--shutdown-timeout`, with a margin for teardown.
+
+- **Pre-stop hook**: Kubernetes removes a terminating pod from the Service endpoints at the same time as it starts terminating the containers, and the removal takes a few seconds to reach every node. The `preStop` sleep delays `SIGTERM` until then. Do not rely on the readiness probe for this: `/health` reports whether the engine is alive, not whether the server is draining. A value of 15 seconds is typically sufficient.
+
+- **Choosing a timeout**: Pick a value that covers most of your requests, for example the p99 of `vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds` from `/metrics`. As a rough guide, 40 seconds is enough to generate about 2000 tokens at 50 tokens/s per request. Increase `--shutdown-timeout`, and `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` with it, for workloads with longer requests.
+
 ## Troubleshooting
 
 ### Startup Probe or Readiness Probe Failure, container log contains "KeyboardInterrupt: terminated"
